#+title: Kubeflow Training Operator v2
#+author: auto-generated reference
#+date: 2026-04-02

* Overview

Kubeflow Training Operator v2 (repo: =kubeflow/trainer=, formerly =kubeflow/training-operator=)
provides a =TrainJob= CRD for submitting training workloads to Kubernetes.

Platform admins define =ClusterTrainingRuntime= resources (GPU defaults, base images,
failure handling). Users submit lightweight =TrainJob= manifests that reference a runtime.

Our use case: submit single-GPU SAE training jobs (=runner.py=) to the cluster
with proper GPU scheduling, secret injection, and shared memory for PyTorch.

* Prerequisites

- Kubernetes >= 1.28 (we run 1.35.1)
- *JobSet CRD* must be installed — Training Operator v2 builds on top of JobSet.
  Check: =kubectl get crds | grep jobset=

* Installation

** Helm (recommended)

Chart is served from an OCI registry — no =helm repo add= needed.

#+begin_src bash
VERSION=2.2.0

# Controller only
helm install kubeflow-trainer oci://ghcr.io/kubeflow/charts/kubeflow-trainer \
    --namespace kubeflow-system \
    --create-namespace \
    --version ${VERSION}

# With built-in runtimes (torch-distributed, deepspeed, etc.)
helm install kubeflow-trainer oci://ghcr.io/kubeflow/charts/kubeflow-trainer \
    --namespace kubeflow-system \
    --create-namespace \
    --version ${VERSION} \
    --set runtimes.defaultEnabled=true

# With specific runtimes only
helm install kubeflow-trainer oci://ghcr.io/kubeflow/charts/kubeflow-trainer \
    --namespace kubeflow-system \
    --create-namespace \
    --version ${VERSION} \
    --set runtimes.torchDistributed.enabled=true
#+end_src

** kubectl alternative

#+begin_src bash
export VERSION=v2.2.0

# Controller
kubectl apply --server-side -k \
  "https://github.com/kubeflow/trainer.git/manifests/overlays/manager?ref=${VERSION}"

# Built-in runtimes
kubectl apply --server-side -k \
  "https://github.com/kubeflow/trainer.git/manifests/overlays/runtimes?ref=${VERSION}"
#+end_src

** Verify

#+begin_src bash
kubectl get crds | grep trainer.kubeflow.org
# Expected:
#   clustertrainingruntimes.trainer.kubeflow.org
#   trainingruntimes.trainer.kubeflow.org
#   trainjobs.trainer.kubeflow.org
#+end_src

* CRDs

| CRD                    | Scope     | Purpose                                        |
|------------------------+-----------+------------------------------------------------|
| ClusterTrainingRuntime | cluster   | Admin-defined template: image, GPU, mlPolicy   |
| TrainingRuntime        | namespace | Same as above but scoped to a namespace        |
| TrainJob               | namespace | User-submitted job referencing a runtime        |

* ClusterTrainingRuntime

Defines the pod template that TrainJobs will use. Admins set the base image,
resource defaults, and ML framework configuration here.

** Built-in =torch-distributed= runtime

This is what ships with the operator when =runtimes.torchDistributed.enabled=true=:

#+begin_src yaml
apiVersion: trainer.kubeflow.org/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterTrainingRuntime
metadata:
  name: torch-distributed
  labels:
    trainer.kubeflow.org/framework: torch
spec:
  mlPolicy:
    numNodes: 1
    torch: {}
  template:
    spec:
      replicatedJobs:
        - name: node
          template:
            metadata:
              labels:
                trainer.kubeflow.org/trainjob-ancestor-step: trainer
            spec:
              template:
                spec:
                  containers:
                    - name: node
                      image: pytorch/pytorch:2.10.0-cuda12.8-cudnn9-runtime
#+end_src

** Custom runtime example

A runtime for single-GPU training with shared memory (needed by PyTorch DataLoader):

#+begin_src yaml
apiVersion: trainer.kubeflow.org/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterTrainingRuntime
metadata:
  name: sae-single-gpu
  labels:
    trainer.kubeflow.org/framework: torch
spec:
  mlPolicy:
    numNodes: 1
  template:
    spec:
      replicatedJobs:
        - name: node
          template:
            metadata:
              labels:
                trainer.kubeflow.org/trainjob-ancestor-step: trainer
            spec:
              template:
                spec:
                  tolerations:
                    - key: nvidia.com/gpu
                      operator: Exists
                      effect: NoSchedule
                  containers:
                    - name: node
                      image: my-training-image:latest
                      resources:
                        requests:
                          memory: "16Gi"
                        limits:
                          nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
                          memory: "32Gi"
                      volumeMounts:
                        - name: dshm
                          mountPath: /dev/shm
                  volumes:
                    - name: dshm
                      emptyDir:
                        medium: Memory
                        sizeLimit: "16Gi"
#+end_src

* TrainJob

Lightweight manifest submitted by users. References a runtime and optionally patches it.

** Minimal

#+begin_src yaml
apiVersion: trainer.kubeflow.org/v1alpha1
kind: TrainJob
metadata:
  name: my-training-run
spec:
  runtimeRef:
    apiGroup: trainer.kubeflow.org
    kind: ClusterTrainingRuntime
    name: sae-single-gpu
#+end_src

** With runtimePatches

=runtimePatches= can add volumes, tolerations, nodeSelector, serviceAccount.
They *cannot* override image, resources, command, args, or env vars for the
=node= container — use the Trainer API for those.

#+begin_src yaml
apiVersion: trainer.kubeflow.org/v1alpha1
kind: TrainJob
metadata:
  name: my-training-run
spec:
  runtimeRef:
    apiGroup: trainer.kubeflow.org
    kind: ClusterTrainingRuntime
    name: sae-single-gpu
  runtimePatches:
    - manager: trainer.kubeflow.org/kubeflow-sdk
      trainingRuntimeSpec:
        template:
          spec:
            replicatedJobs:
              - name: node
                template:
                  spec:
                    template:
                      spec:
                        volumes:
                          - name: training-data
                            persistentVolumeClaim:
                              claimName: my-data-pvc
                        containers:
                          - name: trainer
                            volumeMounts:
                              - name: training-data
                                mountPath: /workspace/data
                        nodeSelector:
                          accelerator: nvidia-tesla-v100
                        tolerations:
                          - key: nvidia.com/gpu
                            operator: Exists
                            effect: NoSchedule
#+end_src

* MLPolicy

Controls distributed training configuration. Set in the runtime's =spec.mlPolicy=.

| Field          | Description                                              |
|----------------+----------------------------------------------------------|
| numNodes       | Number of training nodes (1 for single-GPU)              |
| torch          | Torch-specific config (numProcPerNode, etc.)             |
| mpi            | MPI-specific config (numProcPerNode, implementation)     |
| (empty)        | PlainML — standard K8s Jobs with parallelism = numNodes  |

** Torch policy

#+begin_src yaml
mlPolicy:
  numNodes: 3
  torch:
    numProcPerNode: gpu   # "auto", "gpu", or integer
#+end_src

Uses =torchrun= CLI under the hood. =numProcPerNode: gpu= means one process per GPU.

For single-GPU non-DDP training, just use:

#+begin_src yaml
mlPolicy:
  numNodes: 1
#+end_src

* Planned refactor: unified trainer and dynamic architecture loading

** Problem

Adding a new SAE architecture currently requires changes in 3+ places:

1. =config.py= -- add =TrainerType= enum value, add =TrainerConfig= dataclass,
   add branch in =get_trainer_configs()= if-chain (~200 lines), add top-level
   imports of trainer and SAE classes
2. =utils.py= -- add entry to =_DICT_REGISTRY= (or =_FROM_CONFIG_REGISTRY=),
   add top-level imports of SAE classes
3. Rebuild the training container image (all classes must be baked in)

The trainer classes (10+ of them) are ~95% identical. The =update()= method
follows the same skeleton everywhere:

#+begin_example
def update(self, step, x):
    if step == 0: self.ae.b_dec.data = geometric_median(x)
    x = x.to(self.device)
    loss = self.loss(x, step=step)         # <-- only real variation
    loss.backward()
    remove_gradient_parallel_to_decoder_directions(...)
    clip_grad_norm_(...)
    optimizer.step(); optimizer.zero_grad(); scheduler.step()
    set_decoder_norm_to_unit_norm(...)
    return loss.item()
#+end_example

The only real differences:
- *Loss function* -- sparsity mechanism differs per architecture
- *Decoder weight access* -- =nn.Linear= stores weight as =(activation_dim,
  dict_size)=, =nn.Parameter= stores it as =(dict_size, activation_dim)=.
  Affects 2 lines (gradient projection + norm enforcement). The trainer should
  not care about this: it gets the decoder attribute path as a string, resolves
  it, and infers the convention from the attribute type.
- *Post-step hooks* -- some architectures call =update_annealed_k(step)= or
  =update_annealed_s(step)=. Stiefel skips gradient projection and decoder
  norm entirely (Riemannian optimizer handles manifold constraints).
- *Temporal data shape* -- temporal trainers receive =[batch, 2, d_model]=
  instead of =[batch, d_model]= (stacked adjacent-token pairs).

The =Nested*= trainer variants don't even override =update()= -- they only
override =loss()= from their parent.

** Proposed design

*** Single unified trainer

One trainer class. Parameterized by:

- *Loss class* -- pluggable, loaded by import path. This is where all the
  actual architecture-specific logic lives (sparsity, auxiliary losses,
  threshold updates, dead feature tracking).
- *Decoder attribute path* -- string like ="decoder.weight"= or ="W_dec"=.
  Trainer resolves via =getattr=, infers =nn.Linear= vs =nn.Parameter= from
  the type. Handles transpose automatically.
- *Post-step hooks* -- optional annealing (k, s) and optional skip flags
  for Stiefel (=skip_gradient_projection=, =skip_decoder_norm=).
- Standard training params: =lr=, =seed=, =dict_size=, =k=, =warmup_steps=, etc.
  Note: =k= is common across nearly all architectures.

*** Per-architecture YAML configs

Each architecture gets its own YAML file describing the plumbing:

#+begin_example
# sae_research/training/configs/architectures/batch_top_k.yaml
dict_class: "dictionary_learning.trainers.batch_top_k.BatchTopKSAE"
loss_class: "sae_research.training.losses.BatchTopKLoss"
decoder_attr: "decoder.weight"

defaults:
  auxk_alpha: 0.03125
  threshold_beta: 0.999
  threshold_start_step: 1000
#+end_example

Training run config references architecture by name. =get_trainer_configs()=
if-chain, =TrainerType= enum, and per-architecture =TrainerConfig= dataclasses
all go away.

*** Import-path-based loading (kill _DICT_REGISTRY)

=_DICT_REGISTRY= and =_FROM_CONFIG_REGISTRY= in =utils.py= are replaced by
dotted import paths resolved via =importlib= at load time. The architecture
YAML provides the import path; =load_dictionary()= uses it to get the class.
No top-level imports of architecture classes anywhere.

*** Passing configs to K8s jobs

Architecture YAMLs ship with the =sae_research= package (already in the
container). The training run config is the only thing that varies per job --
passed as a single =config_yaml= string parameter to the KFP component /
TrainJob.

For experimental architectures (arch injection), two additional string params:
=arch_file= (the .py source) and =arch_config_yaml= (the architecture YAML).
Written to =/tmp= at runtime, added to =sys.path=, bundled into the MLflow
artifact via =mlflow.pyfunc.log_model(code_paths=[...])=.

This eliminates the subprocess hack in =train_pipeline.py= -- the component
calls the training function directly.

** Existing tasks affected

- *Self-contained SAE artifacts (mlflow.pyfunc)* -- pyfunc logging bundles
  architecture code with weights, making =_DICT_REGISTRY= unnecessary for
  loading. The unified trainer + pyfunc together close the loop: pyfunc handles
  saving/loading, the architecture YAML handles training config.
- *MLflow pyfunc model logging* -- the =code_paths= mechanism is how injected
  arch files get persisted. Prerequisite for arch injection.
- *Update eval reconciler to use mlflow.pyfunc.load_model* -- once pyfunc is
  the primary artifact format, eval no longer needs the registry either.
- *Support experimental architectures via arch file injection* -- depends on
  the unified trainer (otherwise the injected file would need to provide an
  entire Trainer subclass, not just an SAE class + loss).
- *Fix subprocess hack in train_pipeline.py* -- resolved naturally when the
  KFP component passes a config dict instead of CLI args.
- *YAML-driven training runner* -- the run config YAML is what the unified
  trainer consumes. These tasks merge.
- *Training experiment separation* -- =experiment_name= becomes a field in the
  run config YAML.

** New tasks to add (sketch)

*** Replace =_DICT_REGISTRY= with import-path-based loading
Small, can be done independently. Change =utils.py= =load_dictionary()= to
resolve class from a dotted import path stored in =config.json= (or the
architecture YAML). Remove all top-level architecture imports from =utils.py=.
Backwards-compatible: existing =config.json= files still work via a fallback
that maps class name to import path.

*** Extract loss classes from existing trainers
For each architecture, extract the =loss()= method from the existing trainer
into a standalone loss class. Should be nearly mechanical -- the loss methods
are self-contained. Need to decide what the loss class interface looks like
and where post-step hooks (threshold update, k annealing) live.

*** Unified trainer class
The single trainer that replaces all per-architecture trainers. Takes an SAE
instance, a loss instance, decoder attr path, and skip flags. The =update()=
method is the common skeleton shown above.

*** Per-architecture YAML configs
Move architecture plumbing from Python (=config.py= imports, =TrainerType=
enum, =get_trainer_configs()= if-chain) into YAML files. One file per
architecture.

*** Update training run config format
The run config YAML references an architecture by name and provides sweep
axes. Replaces the current =defaults.yaml= + =demo_config= module globals.
Subsumes the "YAML-driven training runner" task.

** Questions to clarify

*** What does the injected arch file export?
For built-in architectures, the architecture YAML points at specific import
paths for =dict_class= and =loss_class=. For an injected experimental file,
what's the contract? Options:
- The file must define =SAE_CLASS= and =LOSS_CLASS= module-level names
- The file must define classes with specific base classes and we discover them
- The =arch_config_yaml= explicitly names the classes from the file
Third option is most explicit and doesn't require magic names or discovery.

*** Loss class: stateless function or stateful object?
Some losses just compute a tensor (basic reconstruction + sparsity). But
others track running state:
- =update_threshold()= -- maintains a running threshold for activation filtering
- Dead feature tracking -- running count of features that haven't fired
- =update_annealed_k()= / =update_annealed_s()= -- step-dependent annealing
If stateful, the loss object gets initialized with the SAE and maintains its
own state. If stateless, these hooks need to live somewhere else (on the SAE
class? on the trainer?). Where do =scale_biases()= and =update_threshold()=
from =dictionary_learning= SAE classes fit -- are they called from the loss
or from a post-step hook?

*** How to handle dictionary_learning trainer loss methods?
=dictionary_learning= is pinned and its trainers have their own =loss()=
methods. Options:
- Rewrite loss for all architectures (including ones from =dictionary_learning=)
  as standalone loss classes -- clean but duplicates logic
- Wrap the existing =dictionary_learning= trainer's =loss()= method as a loss
  class -- reuses existing code but couples to the external package's internals
- Only use the unified trainer for =sae_research= architectures, keep
  =dictionary_learning= trainers as-is -- avoids the problem but defeats the
  purpose of unification

*** Sweep generation: who owns the sweep axes?
Currently =get_trainer_configs()= has architecture-specific sweep logic
(standard sweeps over =l1_penalty=, top-k over =k=, jump_relu over
=target_l0=). With the unified approach:
- Does the architecture YAML declare which of its params are sweepable and
  what values to try?
- Or is it purely the training run config's job to list sweep axes?
- Or does the architecture YAML declare sweepable params and the run config
  overrides the values?

*** Temporal data shape: trainer or loss concern?
Temporal trainers receive =[batch, 2, d_model]= (adjacent token pairs).
The =update()= skeleton assumes =[batch, d_model]=. Options:
- Temporal loss class handles the slicing internally (receives raw stacked
  input, splits into current/adjacent inside =loss()=)
- Trainer has a preprocessing hook that reshapes before calling loss
- Temporal architectures use a thin trainer subclass that overrides just
  the input handling
First option keeps the trainer fully generic.
